meaning: Browser code tried to use process.env, which only exists in Node. Vite apps expose env vars through import.meta.env instead, so the page crashes with this error.
causes: Code copied from a Next.js or Create React App project uses process.env.REACT_APP_... or process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_....
A library written for Node reads process.env in the browser.
The AI mixed server and client code in one file.

steps.text: Replace process.env with import.meta.env and use the VITE_ prefix.
Rename the vars in .env and in your host's env settings to start with VITE_, then restart the dev server / redeploy.
If a dependency needs it, define it at build time in vite.config.ts.
Never move secret keys to VITE_ variables: anything with VITE_ ends up in the public JavaScript bundle.

prompt: My Vite app crashes with 'ReferenceError: process is not defined'. Replace all browser-side process.env usage with import.meta.env.VITE_*, list the env vars I need to rename in .env and my hosting dashboard, and flag any secret that must move to a server or Edge Function instead of a VITE_ variable.

faq.q: Should I add a process polyfill?
faq.a: Only for a library that truly needs it; for your own code, use import.meta.env.

faq.q: Is my Supabase anon key OK as VITE_?
faq.a: Yes, it's meant to be public (with RLS on). The service_role key is not.
